name: squire
description: Squire is a CLI-first tool for stateless remote validation in clean disposable runtimes.
agent_description: Use Squire when correctness depends on a fresh environment, a specific target runtime, or a short heavy job that is better off your local machine.

commands.name: help
commands.title: Squire Help
commands.summary: show the command catalog or command-specific help
commands.description: Show the top-level Squire command catalog or help for a specific command. This is the canonical discovery surface for humans and agents before choosing a command.
when_to_use: You need to discover the available command surface.
An agent needs structured capability metadata before selecting a tool.
when_not_to_use: You already know the exact command and flags you need.
policy_notes: The richer machine-readable form is available through squire --help --json.

command.description: Optional command path, such as verify or quantum simulate.

help_flags.name: json
help_flags.description: Print the full machine-readable command catalog.

arguments.name: command [subcommand]
arguments.description: Optional command path to show command-specific help.

commands.agent_hint: Start here if you do not already know the correct command or current public-service policy.

commands.name: login
commands.title: Squire Login
commands.summary: authenticate against the Squire API
commands.description: Authenticate the local CLI against the Squire API. Browser-based GitHub OAuth is the default path; headless token login is available for automation and CI.
when_to_use: You are setting up a new machine or shell session.
You need a fresh session token with the latest scopes.
when_not_to_use: You are already logged in and the current session still works.
policy_notes: The default public login flow uses GitHub OAuth.

help_flags.name: token
help_flags.description: Squire-issued headless token for CI or non-browser login.

commands.agent_hint: Use token login for non-interactive automation; otherwise prefer the normal browser flow.

commands.name: update
commands.title: Squire Update
commands.summary: install the latest published Squire CLI
commands.description: Download the published Squire CLI release for the current OS and architecture and replace the local binary in place.
when_to_use: You want the newest published CLI with the latest command surface and fixes.
when_not_to_use: You are developing the CLI locally and want to run the current source tree instead.

help_flags.name: version
help_flags.description: Release tag to install. Defaults to latest.

help_flags.name: install-dir
help_flags.description: Directory to install the binary into.

commands.agent_hint: Use this after install or when help/docs mention behavior your local binary does not have.

commands.name: whoami
commands.title: Squire WhoAmI
commands.summary: show the authenticated user, quotas, and features
commands.description: Return the current authenticated identity, trust tier, feature flags, token metadata, and server-side quotas.
when_to_use: You need to confirm the current trust tier or public feature access.
An agent needs to inspect the current quotas before planning heavier work.
when_not_to_use: You only need to run a command and do not care about session metadata.

help_flags.name: json
help_flags.description: Print the full machine-readable identity and quota payload.

commands.agent_hint: Use before expensive modules if trust tier, quotas, or feature flags matter.

commands.name: logout
commands.title: Squire Logout
commands.summary: clear the local Squire session
commands.description: Remove the locally stored Squire session configuration from the current machine.
when_to_use: You want to clear the current local session.
You are switching between identities on the same machine.
when_not_to_use: You still need the current session token for ongoing work.
commands.agent_hint: Avoid in shared sessions unless the user explicitly wants to clear local auth.

commands.name: mcp
commands.title: Squire MCP
commands.summary: serve the Squire tool surface over MCP stdio
commands.description: Expose the Squire command surface over MCP stdio for clients that expect tool discovery through MCP.
when_to_use: Your host expects MCP tool discovery and stdio transport.
when_not_to_use: A plain terminal workflow is simpler.
commands.agent_hint: Prefer direct CLI use unless an MCP host requires this wrapper.

subcommands.name: serve
subcommands.title: Squire MCP Serve
subcommands.description: Start an MCP stdio server that exposes Squire tools and reuses the current local Squire session.
when_to_use: Your MCP client needs Squire tools over stdio.
when_not_to_use: You only need the normal CLI.
subcommands.agent_hint: This is a local wrapper around the CLI, not a separate remote protocol surface.

commands.name: verify
commands.title: Squire Verify
commands.summary: run shell, Python, or Node checks in fresh Linux runtimes
commands.description: Run small inline snippets or staged scripts in fresh Linux containers across the supported target images.
when_to_use: You need a clean runtime check across Linux targets.
You are debugging OS-sensitive or environment-sensitive behavior.
when_not_to_use: The command is trivial and local execution is faster.
You need a persistent environment or long-running workflow.
policy_notes: Use exact target IDs such as alpine-3.20, ubuntu-24.04, and debian-12.
Outbound network is disabled.

language.description: Language to execute: bash, python, or node.

file.description: Path to a local script file to upload.

targets.description: Target matrix as an array or CSV string.

help_flags.name: lang
help_flags.description: Verify language: bash, python, or node.

commands.agent_hint: Prefer for small runtime repros and environment validation loops before using heavier tools.

commands.name: deps
commands.title: Squire Deps
commands.summary: dependency validation surface; currently disabled on the public zero-egress service
commands.description: Validate whether dependency manifests install in a clean environment. The CLI surface exists, but the public zero-egress service currently rejects deps jobs.
when_to_use: You need dependency-install validation in a clean environment when the service policy allows it.
when_not_to_use: You are targeting the current public service, where deps is disabled.
policy_notes: The current public service rejects deps requests because outbound sandbox network access is not allowed.

file.description: Path to the dependency manifest to upload.

targets.description: Dependency targets as an array or CSV string.

commands.agent_hint: Do not plan around deps on the public service until there is a network-free design for it.
commands.disabled_reason: disabled on the public service under the zero-egress policy

commands.name: sql
commands.title: Squire SQL
commands.summary: run ephemeral SQLite or Postgres validation
commands.description: Run SQLite or Postgres schema, query, and migration validation in a fresh disposable database sandbox.
when_to_use: You need clean SQLite or Postgres validation without local database setup.
when_not_to_use: You need a persistent database or long-lived connection.
policy_notes: Outbound network is disabled.
Postgres runs in a fresh request-scoped helper inside the sandbox.

file.description: Path to a SQL file containing statements to apply.

schema.description: Path to a schema file to apply before the query.

query.description: Inline SQL query to execute after schema setup.

query_file.description: Path to a query file to execute after schema setup.

explain.description: Request an execution plan when the dialect supports it.

help_flags.name: file
help_flags.description: SQL file containing statements to apply.

help_flags.name: schema
help_flags.description: Schema file to apply before a query.

help_flags.name: query-file
help_flags.description: Query file to execute after schema setup.

help_flags.name: explain
help_flags.description: Request an execution plan when supported.

commands.agent_hint: Prefer for schema, migration, and query validation when you want a clean DB per request.

commands.name: test
commands.title: Squire Test
commands.summary: run short clean test suites in fresh runtimes
commands.description: Run small or medium test jobs in clean runtimes with a target matrix for Python, Node, or Bash.
when_to_use: You need a fresh test environment without local drift.
You want a short target matrix instead of full CI.
when_not_to_use: You need a full CI pipeline or long-running test suite.
policy_notes: Outbound network is disabled.

language.description: Test language: python, node, or bash.

files.description: Local file paths to stage for the test run.

command.description: Restricted test command such as pytest -q or npm test.

targets.description: Runtime targets as an array or CSV string.

help_flags.name: file
help_flags.description: File to stage for the test run.

help_flags.name: cmd
help_flags.description: Restricted test command such as pytest -q or npm test.

commands.agent_hint: Prefer for short clean validation loops, not as a replacement for full CI.

commands.name: lint
commands.title: Squire Lint
commands.summary: run lint and static analysis in fresh toolchains
commands.description: Run fixed lint and static-analysis tools in a fresh toolchain so local environment drift does not affect the result.
when_to_use: You need a clean lint result from a fixed supported toolchain.
when_not_to_use: You need arbitrary plugins or unsupported linters.
policy_notes: Outbound network is disabled.
The public service supports ruff, eslint, and clippy.

language.description: Lint language: python, js, ts, or rust.

tool.description: Lint tool: ruff, eslint, or clippy.

files.description: Local file paths to stage for the lint run.

targets.description: Lint targets as an array or CSV string.

examples: squire lint --lang rust --tool clippy --file Cargo.toml --file src/main.rs --json
commands.agent_hint: Prefer when you want a clean supported linter result without local toolchain drift.

commands.name: audit
commands.title: Squire Audit
commands.summary: run dependency, secret, and static security checks
commands.description: Run the supported security-focused audit surfaces against staged local files. On the public service this currently means secret scanning and local-config static analysis.
when_to_use: You need a quick secret scan or a constrained local-config static analysis pass.
when_not_to_use: You need dependency audit on the current public service.
You need remote Semgrep configs or unrestricted external lookups.
policy_notes: The public service supports secret scanning and local-config static analysis.
Dependency audit and remote Semgrep configs are disabled on the public service.
Outbound network is disabled.

language.description: Audit language. Dependency audit is currently disabled publicly.

config.description: Static analysis config as a staged local file path.

paths.description: Local directory paths to stage recursively.

targets.description: Audit targets as an array or CSV string.

help_flags.name: lang
help_flags.description: Dependency audit language. Public dependency audit is currently disabled.

help_flags.name: config
help_flags.description: Static analysis config as a staged local file path.

commands.agent_hint: Use for secret scanning and constrained static checks; do not assume full AppSec platform behavior.

commands.name: build
commands.title: Squire Build
commands.summary: run packaging and build sanity checks
commands.description: Run offline packaging and build sanity checks in clean environments and optionally pull the resulting artifacts back locally.
when_to_use: You want a clean package/build sanity check without publishing anything.
when_not_to_use: You need a full release pipeline or registry publishing.
policy_notes: Outbound network is disabled.
Use --download-artifacts to fetch build outputs locally.

paths.description: Local directory paths to stage recursively.

targets.description: Build targets as an array or CSV string.

download_artifacts_dir.description: Optional local directory to download build artifacts into.

examples: squire build --lang python --file pyproject.toml --path src --targets manylinux,musllinux --download-artifacts ./dist --json

help_flags.name: file
help_flags.description: File to stage for the build.

help_flags.name: download-artifacts
help_flags.description: Local directory to download build artifacts into.

commands.agent_hint: Use when you need the built files back locally but do not want the build to happen on your own machine.

commands.name: bench
commands.title: Squire Bench
commands.summary: run short comparative benchmark jobs
commands.description: Run small, short-lived benchmark jobs in clean runtimes to compare simple timing behavior without turning Squire into a full performance platform.
when_to_use: You want a quick timing comparison in clean runtimes.
when_not_to_use: You need full performance engineering, profiling, or large load tests.
policy_notes: Outbound network is disabled.

language.description: Benchmark language: python, bash, or go.

paths.description: Local directory paths to stage recursively.

targets.description: Benchmark targets as an array or CSV string.

commands.agent_hint: Use for short comparative timing signals, not for full load or saturation testing.

commands.name: browser
commands.title: Squire Browser
commands.summary: run constrained headless browser verification
commands.description: Run headless Chromium in a constrained offline sandbox and optionally download screenshots or other generated browser artifacts locally.
when_to_use: You need offline browser verification against staged local assets.
You need screenshots or simple DOM/assertion checks in a disposable browser runtime.
when_not_to_use: You need to fetch remote http:// or https:// URLs on the public service.
policy_notes: The public service is offline-only for browser runs.
Stage full local asset trees with --path when you need images, fonts, or other binary files.
Use --download-artifacts to fetch screenshots or other generated files locally.

download_artifacts_dir.description: Optional local directory to download screenshots or other browser artifacts into.

help_flags.name: url
help_flags.description: Offline URL to open, such as file://.

help_flags.name: file
help_flags.description: File to stage for browser execution.

help_flags.name: download-artifacts
help_flags.description: Local directory to download screenshots or other browser artifacts into.

commands.agent_hint: Use staged local assets and artifact downloads. Do not plan around remote URLs on the public service.

commands.name: compile
commands.title: Squire Compile
commands.summary: check Go or Rust compilation for target environments
commands.description: Run target-specific Go or Rust compilation checks in clean toolchains without turning Squire into a full CI or release system.
when_to_use: You need target compilation validation in a clean environment.
when_not_to_use: You need full repository builds or arbitrary Docker-based build systems.
policy_notes: Outbound network is disabled.

files.description: Local file paths to stage for compilation.

targets.description: Compile targets as an array or CSV string.

examples: squire compile --lang rust --file Cargo.toml --file src/main.rs --targets linux/amd64-musl,linux/arm64 --json

commands.name: solve
commands.title: Squire Solve
commands.summary: run Z3 or MiniZinc solver jobs
commands.description: Run bounded solver jobs for Z3 or MiniZinc in a fresh disposable sandbox.
when_to_use: You need a satisfiability or small optimization/model check without local solver setup.
when_not_to_use: You need arbitrary scripting around solvers or long-running research workloads.
policy_notes: Outbound network is disabled.

file.description: Path to the solver input file.

commands.agent_hint: Use for bounded solver tasks where structured SAT/UNSAT output matters.

commands.name: quantum
commands.title: Squire Quantum
commands.summary: run offline Qiskit Aer simulations in a dedicated runtime
commands.description: Run bounded offline quantum simulations in a dedicated Qiskit Aer runtime.
when_to_use: You need an offline Qiskit Aer simulation in a fresh remote runtime.
when_not_to_use: You need notebooks, persistent sessions, hardware providers, or multiple frameworks.
policy_notes: Quantum runs are offline-only on the public service.
Trusted access or higher is currently required.
commands.agent_hint: Treat this as a narrow offline simulation surface, not a general quantum platform.

subcommands.name: simulate
subcommands.title: Squire Quantum Simulate
subcommands.summary: run an offline Qiskit Aer simulation in a dedicated runtime
subcommands.description: Stage a small Python/Qiskit file set, run the entry file inside an offline Qiskit Aer image, and optionally download generated artifacts locally.
when_to_use: You need bounded Qiskit Aer simulation and the local job is too heavy or noisy.
when_not_to_use: You need hardware providers, notebooks, or persistent sessions.
policy_notes: The first --file is the Python entry script.
Additional --file values stage helper modules or local assets.
Write files under /workspace/output and use --download-artifacts to retrieve them locally.
The public service is offline-only and trusted-only for this module.

files.description: Local file paths to stage. The first file is the Python entry script.

shots.description: Shot count passed to the simulation.

backend.description: Quantum backend. v1 supports only aer_simulator.

download_artifacts_dir.description: Optional local directory to download generated quantum artifacts into.

help_flags.name: shots
help_flags.description: Shot count passed to the simulation.

help_flags.name: download-artifacts
help_flags.description: Local directory to download generated quantum artifacts into.

subcommands.agent_hint: Use for bounded offline simulations only, and plan around trusted-only public access.

commands.name: data
commands.title: Squire Data
commands.summary: run Python data jobs with pandas, polars, or pyarrow

Outbound network is disabled.

when_not_to_use: You are writing new command invocations.
